case_title: JITUL JENTILAL KOTECHA v. STATE OF GUJARAT AND ORS.
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the appellant, purchased a property from Shamjibhai Jesabhai Koli and executed an agreement to sell. The appellant and his family members paid the consideration for the property. The daughters of Shamjibhai, who were the second and third respondents, instituted a civil suit to cancel the sale deed. The second and third respondents executed powers of attorney and Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with other individuals, including the sixth and seventh respondents, for the sale of the property. The appellant filed an FIR against the respondents for alleged offenses under sections 465, 467, 468, and 120B of the IPC. The High Court quashed the FIR against most of the accused, except for the fourth and fifth respondents, who were alleged to have committed the offense of extortion under section 385 of the IPC. The High Court's decision was challenged, and the Supreme Court set aside the High Court's order, allowing the criminal appeals and dismissing the quashing petitions.
